narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found a 59% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a figure that, while not overwhelmingly high, was sufficient to result in a denial. This means the decision was not clear-cut, and your profile contains both concerning and reassuring elements that together tipped the outcome in an unfavorable direction.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about one in five had a negative checking account balance, while roughly half of approved applicants had no such deficit at all. A negative balance signals to the assessment that your day-to-day finances may already be under strain, which raises concerns about your ability to take on additional debt obligations.

On a more positive note, the duration of your requested loan — 12 months — actually worked in your favor. Approved applicants took out loans lasting nearly 20 months on average, so your shorter repayment period suggests a more modest and manageable commitment, and this was recognized as a reassuring sign.

However, your savings situation added further concern. With less than 100 DM in savings, you fall into the same category as just over half of approved applicants, so this alone is not unusual — but combined with a negative checking account balance, it reinforces the picture of limited financial reserves. Having little cushion in savings alongside an already strained checking account makes it harder to demonstrate that you could weather unexpected financial difficulties during the loan period.

It is also worth noting that your requested loan amount of 795 DM is well below the average of nearly 2,900 DM among approved applicants, and your loan purpose — education — is among the less common reasons for approved loans. These factors did not drive the decision as strongly, but they form part of the broader context.

To improve your chances in a future application, the most impactful step you could take would be to bring your checking account into a positive balance and maintain it there for a period before reapplying. Building up your savings, even modestly, would further strengthen your profile. Given that your requested amount is relatively small and your repayment term is short, addressing the checking account situation in particular could meaningfully shift the outcome in your favor.
